BalanceWarning.description: Advisory only, and absent while the balance is healthy. Sent on every authenticated response (the OpenAI-compatible inference endpoints excepted) while the organization has machines running, auto-pay is off or its last charge failed, and the balance covers less than the low-balance threshold (2 hours by default) at the current usage. Plain text, for example "Your balance covers about 1.5 hours at your current usage. Machines stop when it reaches $0. Add funds or turn on auto-pay: https://gpu.ai/cloud/billing?tab=credits&autopay=1". It never changes the request. The same condition sends the balance.low webhook.

ZeroDataRetentionHeader.description: Send `true` to require zero data retention for this request even when the org setting is off. It can only tighten routing: `false` never relaxes an org with zero data retention on. Responses routed under zero data retention echo this header with `true`. A model without a zero-data-retention host returns 400 `zero_data_retention_unavailable`; a value other than true/false returns 400 `invalid_header`.
ZeroDataRetentionHeader.name: X-GPUAI-Zero-Data-Retention

auto_terminate_hours.description: Terminate this instance automatically after this many hours of runtime. Omit for no limit (the default). The countdown starts when the instance reaches `running`, not when you call this — provisioning is neither billed nor counted against the limit — and the resolved deadline is returned as `auto_terminate_at` on every read. Enforcement is server-side and survives your process: this is the safety net for an unattended run whose client dies without cleaning up. When it fires the instance is terminated exactly as a DELETE would terminate it (billing stops, the `instance.terminated` webhook fires) and `status_reason` records that the limit was reached. Bounds: at least 1, at most 720 (30 days) — outside them returns 422 `validation_failed`. An explicit `0` is rejected rather than read as "no limit"; omit the field for that.

cmd.description: Override the image's CMD. Omit to use the image's own (or none, when `entrypoint` is overridden with a non-empty argv; an empty-array entrypoint clear keeps the image CMD). An explicit empty array clears the CMD. Empty strings inside a non-empty argv are rejected (422). Requires `image`.

dedicated_ip.description: Attach a dedicated public IPv4 address owned by GPU.ai. Its inbound TCP ports (80 and 443 unless `ports` says otherwise) forward, raw and without TLS termination, to the same ports on the instance's loopback, so your own certificates work. Billed hourly while attached plus per GB of transfer in both directions (see GET /dedicated-ip). on_demand tier only (422 `validation_failed` otherwise). Returns 409 `dedicated_ip_limit` when the organization already holds its limit, 503 `dedicated_ip_unavailable` when no address is free, 422 `validation_failed` for ports outside the allowed set, and 400 `validation_failed` on deployments where the add-on is not enabled. A launch whose address cannot be attached fails its operation with `dedicated_ip_unavailable`. The address is released when the instance terminates or fails.

disk_gb.description: Requested instance filesystem size in GB. Omit for the platform default (100 GB), which never narrows placement. Setting it is a hard requirement: placement narrows to capacity that can honor it (see `disk_configurable` on GET /v1/pricing), and a request no offering of the gpu_type can honor returns 422 `disk_unavailable` rather than launching with a different size. When the launch also pins an exact `offering_id`, a disk_gb larger than that offering's displayed `storage_gb` returns 422 `disk_exceeds_offering` rather than launching with a clamped filesystem. Disk beyond the included allowance (100 GB) is billed at the offering's `disk_price_per_gb_hour` (GET /v1/pricing), folded into the instance's single hourly rate. Bounds: at least 10, at most the platform ceiling (currently 1000) — outside them returns 422 `validation_failed`.

entrypoint.description: Override the image's ENTRYPOINT (docker semantics — also drops the image CMD unless `cmd` is given). Omit to use the image's own; an explicit empty array clears it while keeping the image CMD (docker `--entrypoint ""` semantics). Empty strings inside a non-empty argv are rejected (422). At most 32 arguments / 4KB. Requires `image`.

env.description: Environment variables. With `template_id`: per-deploy overrides — only keys the template marks user_overridable are accepted (others 422), and secret values are redacted from operation metadata. With `image`: plain container env vars — keys must be POSIX names and the platform's reserved namespace (`PUBLIC_KEY`, `GPUAI_*`) is refused (422).

environment.description: Launch environment. Omit for the provider default (the GPU.ai Certified Image where supported). Accepted values: `certified` (the GPU.ai Certified base image), `certified:<framework>` (a framework layer — see GET /v1/environments for the roster, e.g. `certified:pytorch`), `certified:<framework>@<version>` (a specific framework version, e.g. `certified:pytorch@2.13`), `raw_vm` (root VM, provider default OS), `raw_vm:<os>` (root VM with a chosen OS, e.g. `raw_vm:ubuntu-24.04`), or `provider_template` (the provider's own image). A well-formed value the placed machine can't serve returns 422 `environment_unavailable`.

image.description: Launch from your own container image, e.g. `pytorch/pytorch:2.4.1-cuda12.4-cudnn9-devel` or `ghcr.io/acme/trainer:v1`. The image must be publicly pullable (private registries are not yet supported) and provide linux/amd64 — both are verified synchronously before anything is provisioned: an unknown image returns 422 `image_unavailable` and a registry outage 502 `registry_unreachable`, with no operation created and nothing billed. The launch is pinned to the exact manifest digest verified, so a tag re-push cannot change what boots. After SSH/tunnel setup the image's own ENTRYPOINT/CMD is started (its output is in /var/log/gpuai-entrypoint.log on the instance); an image with neither is a plain SSH environment. Placement prefers container-native capacity (the image runs natively; SSH lands inside it) and falls back to VM capacity (the image runs as a container beside the host's SSH — inspect with `docker logs gpuai-workload`); private images stay container-native. A gpu_type with no capable capacity returns 422 `image_unavailable`. Mutually exclusive with `template_id` and `environment` (422). A malformed reference (bad charset, localhost/private-IP registry) returns 400. On-demand only for now: `tier: spot` with `image` is refused (422 `validation_failed`) because a preemption re-route cannot yet carry a custom image.

max_price_per_hour.description: maximum acceptable whole-instance hourly price (catalog price)

offering_id.description: Pin the launch to one exact offering (from GET /v1/pricing) so the engine never substitutes a pricier one. If that offering is gone, the launch fails explicitly rather than silently placing elsewhere.

ports.description: Container ports to expose on a custom-image launch (at most 10; port 22 is reserved). At most one entry may be `primary` — it must be http and is served at the instance's app URL (`https://<id>.apps.gpu.ai`) behind the per-instance basic-auth login. Requires `image`.

registry_credential_id.description: Stored registry-credential id (POST /v1/registry-credentials) for pulling a PRIVATE `image`. The credential's registry must match the image's registry (422 otherwise); wrong logins fail the pre-flight with 422 `image_unavailable` before anything is provisioned. Requires `image`.

secrets.description: Names of organization secrets (POST /secrets) to deliver to the machine at boot as environment variables of the same names. Values are never in a response or a log. Returns 422 `validation_failed` when a name does not exist or secrets are not enabled on this deployment.

template_id.description: Deploy a curated application template (e.g. comfyui, vllm). When set, gpu_type may be omitted — the cheapest eligible GPU is auto-selected. For templates serving a Hugging Face model via env.MODEL (vllm, sglang), the model's published weights size is checked against the GPU's VRAM at submit time: an oversized model on an explicit gpu_type returns 422 `model_too_large` (auto-select instead raises its VRAM floor to the estimate, and 422s only when no available GPU fits). Gated/private/unknown repos are never blocked — the deploy proceeds and the 202 carries a `warnings` entry. Separately, an explicit gpu_type whose VRAM is below the template's own `min_vram_gb` returns 422 `gpu_vram_too_small`, naming the floor, the type's VRAM and the compatible GPU types. Auto-select is unaffected — it already filters by the floor.

tier.description: `spot` is soft-deprecated: spot capacity is currently unavailable sitewide (requests with tier=spot return no offerings); use on_demand.

viewed_price_per_hour.description: The retail $/hr the caller displayed to the user before launch. A catalog row is a quote, not a booking, and pinning an offering fixes which machine is placed but not its rate. If the launch-time price exceeds this by more than $0.01 the launch fails with `price_changed` carrying the new price instead of proceeding at the higher price; omit to accept the launch-time price (previous behavior). Refusal only — it is never read as consent, so it can neither raise what you are charged nor widen what may be bought on your behalf. Use max_price_per_hour to bound spend.

OpenAIBadGateway.description: The upstream answered but its response could not be used (OpenAI error envelope): code upstream_response_too_large when the vector payload exceeded the per-request size limit, or upstream_error for a malformed / misaligned response. Not retryable as-is for upstream_response_too_large — send fewer inputs.

OpenAIBadRequest.description: Invalid request (OpenAI error envelope). On inference routes this includes `zero_data_retention_unavailable` when zero data retention is required and the model has no zero-data-retention host.

OpenAIForbidden.description: API key lacks the required scope (OpenAI error envelope).

OpenAIGone.description: The requested artifact has expired and is no longer available (OpenAI error envelope).

OpenAINotFound.description: Model or resource not found (OpenAI error envelope).

OpenAIRateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded (OpenAI error envelope). Retry-After header indicates seconds to wait.

Retry-After.description: Seconds the client should wait before retrying.

OpenAIRequestTooLarge.description: Request body too large (OpenAI error envelope, code request_too_large).

OpenAIUnauthorized.description: Missing or invalid API key (OpenAI error envelope).

OpenAIUpstreamTimeout.description:
Upstream provider exceeded the synchronous per-attempt deadline (OpenAI
error envelope). 504 semantic — distinct from 503 OpenAIUpstreamUnavailable
which signals a connection or routing failure rather than a timeout.

OpenAIUpstreamUnavailable.description: Upstream provider unavailable (OpenAI error envelope). Retry-After header may indicate seconds to wait. Code `data_retention_check_failed` means the org zero data retention setting could not be read, so the request was not sent; retry shortly.

Retry-After.description: Seconds the client should wait before retrying.

OpenAIVideoList.description: A page of video generation jobs.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded (RFC 7807). Retry-After header indicates seconds to wait.

Retry-After.description: Seconds the client should wait before retrying.

AutolaunchLaunchSpec.description:
The full create-instance body this rule freezes and replays — the same shape POST /v1/instances accepts. It is modelled as an open object rather than a $ref because the instance-create body is an inline requestBody schema rather than a named component; promoting it would rewrite the instances operation and every generated client's signature for it, in a change that only needs to STORE one.

Two fields behave differently here than on a live create: `offering_id` is REJECTED (a pinned offering produces a rule that can never fire, because offering identity churns between catalog polls), and `auto_terminate_hours` is OVERWRITTEN from the rule's `max_runtime_hours` so a nested field cannot widen the runtime bound the customer approved.

AutolaunchRule.description: A standing, pre-approved purchase order. It carries no upstream supplier identity, no org id, and no identifier of the API key that consented — the consenting principal is recorded in storage for the fire-time re-check, and a credential identifier has no business in a rule listing.

attempts_this_edge.description: Launch attempts made since the current condition edge began.

capacity_class.description: Capacity class the rule is narrowed to, or null for both.

created_by_surface.description: Which entrance consented. A dashboard rule has no API key behind it, which is why its fire-time revocation failure is `authority_revoked` (the approving admin was demoted) rather than `key_revoked`.

enabled.description: False once disarmed or cancelled. A disarmed rule cannot be re-armed.

gpu_model.description: The canonical GPU model id the rule targets and launches, e.g. "h100_sxm" — a MODEL, not a generation. "H100" names three differently priced SKUs, matches nothing in the catalog, and is refused: a rule that can never fire is a standing purchase order the customer believes is armed. Case and punctuation are forgiving ("RTX-A4000" resolves to "rtx_a4000") and the canonical id is what is stored. It must also match spec.gpu_type, or the rule would wait on one market and buy from another.

last_failure_reason.description: Why the last attempt did not buy anything: over_ceiling, capacity_race, stale_reference, key_revoked, authority_revoked or validation_failed, optionally with a colon-separated detail. Match the leading token. It never carries API key material.

launched_instance_id.description: The instance this rule launched, once it has fired — an instance id of the form "gpu-" + 8 lowercase hex, the same string /v1/instances returns. Not a uuid, and deliberately carries no format or pattern: no other instance-id field in this document constrains its shape, and a generated client-side assertion on an id grammar turns a server-side widening into a client-side outage.

max_price_per_hour.description: The CEILING, and the consent. Dollars per hour for the WHOLE INSTANCE, not per GPU. The launch is abandoned — never repriced — if the live price exceeds it.

max_runtime_hours.description: How long an auto-launched instance may run before the platform terminates it, enforced through the instance's own auto_terminate_hours.

max_total_usd.description: The worst-case total the customer approved: max_price_per_hour × max_runtime_hours, computed by the server and echoed on every read so a client never has to derive the number it is displaying.

region.description: Canonical region the rule is narrowed to, or null for every region.

spec.description:
The frozen launch spec, as READ. Every value under `env` is returned as the literal `[REDACTED]` — the key names are kept so you can see what the launch will set, but the values are not readable back on any surface, by any scope. Reading a rule needs only `autolaunch:read`, which every full_access, standard and read_only key holds, so a rule listing must not be a credential listing.
This changes nothing about what the rule DOES: the stored spec keeps the real values and replays them at fire time. If you need to change a token, delete the rule and create a new one.

state.description: armed = waiting for the condition. launching = an attempt is in flight. fired = a successful launch consumed the rule's one shot. expired = the per-edge attempt budget ran out. A lost capacity race costs nothing and does NOT consume the shot.

threshold.description: The TRIGGER. Dollars PER GPU-HOUR for price_under, or a unit count for count_at_least. Null for in_stock. This is NOT the spend cap — see max_price_per_hour, which is in a different unit.

acknowledged_max_total_usd.description: REQUIRED. Echo of the worst-case total, max_price_per_hour × max_runtime_hours, accepted within one cent. This is the consent gate: a caller that never computed this number cannot have shown it to the person approving the rule, and a caller that displayed a different number disagrees with what is about to be stored. Either way the request is refused so the caller can re-render the real figure.

capacity_class.description: Omit or send null to consider both capacity classes.

max_price_per_hour.description: The CEILING, in dollars per hour for the WHOLE INSTANCE. Required even for in_stock rules: "buy it when it comes back" with no ceiling is an unbounded authorization, and this resource has no such shape. Values above the maximum are refused with a 422 naming the bound.

region.description: Omit or send null to consider every region.

threshold.description: The TRIGGER, in dollars PER GPU-HOUR for price_under or a unit count for count_at_least. Required and greater than zero for both. Ignored for in_stock. Not the spend cap. Values above the maximum are refused with a 422 naming the bound — it is the largest value the column stores.

AutolaunchRuleDisarm.description: The entire PATCH surface. `enabled` must be present and must be false. Any other key is refused rather than accepted-and-ignored, because a PATCH carrying a new ceiling that returned 200 would leave the caller believing the cap had moved.

enabled.description: Must be false. Sending true is refused: a fired rule consumed its one shot, so "resume" would silently be an authorization nobody gave, and arming again is a create.

Balance.description: The organization's credit balance with its auto-pay configuration and live burn rate. Mirrors the dashboard's balance contract field for field. No payment-instrument detail appears here — saved cards live behind separate admin-only routes.

auto_pay_amount_cents.description: Amount auto-pay charges when it triggers. Meaningful only when auto_pay_enabled.

auto_pay_threshold_cents.description: Auto-pay triggers when the balance falls below this. Meaningful only when auto_pay_enabled.

balance_cents.description: Remaining credit in USD cents. May be negative when usage has outrun the balance.

balance_dollars.description: The same figure in dollars, for display.

burn_cents_per_hour.description:
Live burn rate in USD cents per hour: the committed hourly price of every instance that is live, counted from launch — so instances still creating, provisioning or booting are included, not only those that have reached running. 0 when nothing is live.

`null` means the burn rate could not be determined. Treat that as unknown, never as 0: reading an unavailable burn rate as "nothing running" reports unbounded runway to an organization that may be minutes from empty.

runway_hours.description: How many hours the balance lasts at the current usage: the balance divided by `burn_cents_per_hour` plus serverless inference spend over the last hour, rounded to 2 places. `null` when nothing is running or the burn rate could not be determined; 0 when the balance is at or below $0 while burning. Machines stop when the balance reaches $0.

tax_id_enabled.description: False when this deployment cannot store a Tax ID.

tax_id_masked.description: The stored Tax ID, masked. Empty when none is stored.

tax_id_type.description: eu_vat, gb_vat, ch_vat, no_vat, us_ein, ca_bn, au_abn, nz_gst, in_gst, sg_uen, jp_cn, kr_brn, ae_trn, sa_vat, br_cnpj, mx_rfc or other. Empty when no Tax ID is stored.

deposit_id.description: Stripe PaymentIntent id (saved card) or Checkout Session id (checkout).

status.description: succeeded = charged, credited by webhook within seconds. processing = the issuer has not settled yet. requires_action = open `action_url` to finish 3-D Secure. awaiting_payment = open `checkout_url` to pay.

match.description: The deposit-match promotion's decision, once credited (absent when no promotion applied).

hold_until.description: Card deposits' match is held until this time before it can be released.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether the model may call several tools in one turn. Passed through.

tool_choice.description: "auto" (default), "none", "required", or a named function ({"type":"function","function":{"name":"..."}}) that must be defined in tools.

tools.description: Functions the model may call (OpenAI shape). Only models whose /v1/models entry has supports_tools: true accept it; any other model returns 400 unsupported_parameter (param "tools").

model.description: Canonical (gpuai/...) model id, NEVER the upstream HF path.

content.description: Message text. null on an assistant message that only calls tools. Requests may also send an array of content parts, passed through unchanged.

tool_call_id.description: The tool call this message answers (required on role "tool").

tool_calls.description: Tool calls made by the assistant (assistant messages only).

ChatResponseFormat.description: Structured outputs. {"type":"json_object"} (JSON mode) or {"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{...}}; "text" is the default. Only models whose /v1/models entry has supports_structured_outputs: true accept json_object / json_schema.

arguments.description: JSON-encoded arguments object, as a string.

parameters.description: JSON Schema for the function arguments.

cost.description: What the cluster's machines have cost so far, in USD.

demand_gpus.description: GPU work waiting for a machine.

price_per_hour.description: What the cluster's machines cost now, per hour. Machines being released are not counted; a deleted cluster's price is 0.

gpu_type.description: GPU type of every machine; see GET /gpu-types.

idle_timeout.description: Seconds a machine may run no GPU work before it is removed (down to min_nodes).

max_nodes.description: Most machines under load. Defaults to min_nodes.

max_price_per_hour.description: Highest hourly price per machine, in USD.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter (32 at most).

placement.description: "spread" places machines on different suppliers where it can.

regions.description: Canonical regions to place machines in. Empty means the cheapest suitable listing anywhere.

address.description: The machine's address on the cluster network.

terminating.description: Machines being released. A deleted cluster is `deleting` until this is 0.

gpu_limit.description: Most GPUs the queue may use (-1 no limit).

gpu_quota.description: GPUs the queue is guaranteed (-1 none).

unpaid_cents.description: Accrued but not yet paid out, in cents.

CommunityMachine.description: A self-declared Community Cloud machine. Spec fields are optional and unverified until Phase 57. The enrollment token hash is never serialized.

tier.description: Supplier-chosen rental model. on_demand = guaranteed whole-node capacity; spot = cheaper interruptible capacity. Defaults to on_demand. Becomes the catalog offering's tier.

CommunityMachineDelistResult.description: The terminal status a machine reached after a delist. `draining` means it was occupied and the existing rental keeps running (never killed); `delisted` means it was idle and left supply immediately.

enrollment_token.description: One-time enrollment token — shown exactly once, store securely.

CommunitySupplier.description: One organization's Community Cloud supplier profile (ONBD-01).

CreateFineTuningJobRequest.description: Request body for POST /fine_tuning/jobs. The `method` object carries the Axolotl LoRA/QLoRA hyperparameters; `gpuai` is a native extension for the optional budget cap and GPU preference. The backing training environment (image, GPU provider) is an internal orchestration detail and is intentionally absent from this schema (privacy-by-omission, D6).

model.description: An operator-curated tunable base model id.

training_file.description: The id of a previously uploaded file (purpose=fine-tune).

name.description: A letter, then letters, digits, underscores or hyphens; 63 characters at most.

input.description: The pickled (args, kwargs) of the call, base64-encoded. 4 MB at most before encoding.

version_id.description: The version to run. Omit to run the function's current version.

bundle_bytes.description: Size of the pickled function. 64 MB at most.

bundle_sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the pickled function.

content_hash.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 over the code and everything declared about it.

gpu.description: A GPU type from GET /gpu-types. Omit to use the cheapest GPU that fits.

idle_timeout.description: Seconds a machine stays ready after a call. 0 releases it at once.

min_vram_gb.description: Least VRAM per GPU, used when gpu is omitted.

pip.description: Requirements to install on the machine. Options (anything starting with "-") are refused.

python_version.description: The Python minor version the function was pickled with, such as "3.11".

secrets.description: Names of organization secrets (POST /secrets) each run receives as environment variables of the same names, resolved per call so a rotated value reaches the next call. Values are never in a response or a log. Returns 422 `validation_failed` when a name does not exist or secrets are not enabled on this deployment.

timeout.description: Seconds one call may run. 1 to 86400.

CryptoDeposit.description: A stablecoin deposit. Mirrors the Go DTO field for field. Like that struct, this schema deliberately has NO payment-processor property — the processor is an implementation detail and is structurally absent from the customer contract, not merely filtered out.

amount_usd_cents.description: The amount requested, in USD cents. Never the settled or credited value.

credited_cents.description: USD cents actually credited to the balance. Absent until credited.

expires_at.description: RFC3339 UTC. After this, send nothing to pay_address.

pay_address.description: The address to send funds to. Unique to this deposit.

pay_amount.description: The exact token amount to send, as a decimal string (never a number — the value must not round-trip through a float).

status.description: Lifecycle state: created, detected, confirming, settled, screening, held_screening, credited, credited_underpaid, credited_overpaid, expired, expired_received, failed, failed_screening.

updated_at.description: When the setting last changed; absent if it never has.

zero_data_retention.description: True when the org's inference requests route only to zero-data-retention model hosts.

acceptable_use.description: The acceptable use policy for dedicated IPs.

allowed_ports.description: Ports and port ranges a launch may forward, e.g. `80,443,1024-65535`.

available.description: Addresses free for a new launch right now.

default_ports.description: Ports forwarded when the request names none.

hourly_fee.description: USD per hour while attached, from the instance becoming running until release.

max_ports.description: Most ports one address may forward.

org_in_use.description: Dedicated IPs the organization holds now.

org_limit.description: Most dedicated IPs the organization may hold at once.

transfer_cap_gb.description: GB per attachment after which forwarding is suspended.

transfer_included_gb.description: GB of transfer per attachment that is not charged.

transfer_price_per_gb.description: USD per GB through the address, inbound and outbound.

DedicatedIPRequest.description: Requests a dedicated public IPv4 address for the instance. Send an empty object for the default ports (80 and 443).

ports.description: Inbound TCP ports to forward. Each must be in the deployment's allowed set (see GET /dedicated-ip). Port 22 and the gateway's own ports are never allowed; SSH stays on the instance's SSH command. Omit for the defaults.

index.description: Position of this vector's input in the request.

dimensions.description: Requested output dimensionality, for models that support truncated (Matryoshka) embeddings. Passed through to the model when set.

encoding_format.description: Only "float" is supported. A value of "base64" is rejected with invalid_request_error / unsupported_parameter.

input.description: Text to embed: either a single string or an array of up to 2048 strings. Token-id arrays are not supported. The per-request ceiling is bounded so the response stays under 64 MiB — about 680 inputs at 4096 dimensions, fewer at a larger `dimensions` value; an over-limit batch is rejected with 400 invalid_request_error whose message states the limit, before any processing.

user.description: Opaque end-user identifier for abuse tracing. Optional.

model.description: Canonical (gpuai/...) model id, NEVER the upstream identifier.

EmbeddingsUsage.description: Embeddings are billed on input tokens only, so this block carries no completion_tokens field — an embeddings call emits none, and total_tokens always equals prompt_tokens.

last_error.description: Why the latest machine failed to start, until one becomes ready.

machines.description: Recent machines, newest first. Returned by GET /v1/endpoints/{id} only.

url.description: OpenAI-compatible base URL. Set an OpenAI client's base_url to it and use a GPU.ai API key.

gpu_type.description: The GPU each machine runs on (see GET /v1/gpu-types). At least 24 GB of memory.

hf_token_secret.description: Name of an organization secret holding a Hugging Face token, delivered as HF_TOKEN (for gated models).

idle_timeout.description: Seconds without a request before a machine is released. Default 300.

max_price_per_hour.description: Highest hourly price for a machine.

max_replicas.description: Most machines the endpoint scales out to. Default 1.

min_replicas.description: Machines kept running even with no requests. Default 0 (scale to zero).

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter; 48 characters at most. Unique among the organization's endpoints.

target_concurrency.description: In-flight requests per machine before another starts. Default 16.

instance_id.description: The instance the machine runs as (it appears in the instance list as ep-<name>-<id>).

frameworks.description: Certified framework ids whose images are fully published — the `certified:<framework>` options.

includes.description: "What's included" software lists: framework id (roster ids plus "base") → CUDA variant ("cuda128"/"cuda124") → components.

versions.description: The version picker roster: framework id → selectable versions (the `certified:<framework>@<version>` grammar). A framework absent here has one build per CUDA variant. `variant` is the CUDA variant a version targets — only offerings whose GPU maps to it can run it.

vm_images.description: The raw-VM OS catalog (the `raw_vm:<os>` grammar), keyed by os id.

FileObject.description: An uploaded file object. The storage location is an internal detail and is intentionally absent from this schema (privacy-by-omission, D6).

FineTuningJob.description: The fine-tuning job object. `status` is the COLLAPSED public enum (the rich internal states are hidden). `result_files` are freshly-presigned, short-lived download URLs regenerated per read. No backing-provider identity is present (D6).

fine_tuned_model.description: Null in this release (catalog auto-serve is a later phase).

finished_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) at terminal state; null until terminal.

default.description: Preselected in the picker (at most one per framework).

Function.description: A Python function registered with GPU.ai. The settings are those of its current version and are null until the first version is uploaded.

gpu.description: The GPU type, or null when the cheapest GPU that fits is used.

idle_timeout.description: Seconds a machine stays ready after a call.

machine_cost_24h_usd.description: What the function's machines were billed in the last 24 hours, including start-up and idle time that belongs to no run.

max_concurrency.description: Most machines running calls at once.

run_cost_24h_usd.description: Sum of the cost of the runs created in the last 24 hours.

status.description: `running`: a call is executing. `warm`: a machine is ready and waiting. `starting`: a machine is being started. `idle`: no machine, nothing is billed.

timeout.description: Seconds one call may run before it is stopped.

FunctionReplicaCounts.description: How many machines a function has in each state.

warm.description: Machines ready and waiting for a call.

cold_start.description: True when the call waited for a machine to start, false when a warm machine took it.

cost_usd.description: The time the call held its machine, at the machine's hourly price. Machine time between calls is billed too but belongs to no call.

duration_ms.description: How long the function body ran.

instance_id.description: The machine that ran the call. It is an instance of the organization.

result.description: The pickled return value, base64-encoded. Present only on a succeeded run fetched with include_result=true.

status.description: queued waits for a machine; setting_up means a machine took the call and is installing the function's Python and pip requirements; running means the function body is executing.

traceback.description: The remote traceback, when the function raised.

type.description: The class name of the exception the function raised, or the platform's reason: Timeout, Cancelled, LaunchError, MachineLost, DependencyError and so on.

stream.description: system carries messages from the platform, such as dependency installation.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `after` on the next read.

run_status.description: The run's status at read time. Once it is final and data is empty, there is no more output.

url.description: Where to send the pickled function.

secrets.description: Names of the organization secrets each run receives. Empty when none.

upload.description: Present while the bundle still has to be uploaded.

stock_known.description: False when the live catalog could not be read; nothing is then refused for capacity.

price_per_hour.description: Cheapest machine in stock, USD per hour for the whole machine; 0 when not in stock.

vm_in_stock.description: In stock as a whole VM, where launches place first; price_per_hour is then the VM price.

cpu_cores.description: Representative host vCPU count for this GPU model. Unlike vram_gb (the card's nameplate VRAM; a model spanning capacity variants advertises the smallest currently offered, so it is the value every launch of the model can honor) this varies per offering, so it is the first-sighting/typical value; GET /v1/pricing carries the exact per-offering spec. 0 marks a spec the upstream did not report.

disk_configurable.description: true when at least one offering of this model accepts a custom disk_gb at launch (an OR across offerings — requesting disk_gb narrows placement to the capable capacity).

instance_disk_gb.description: Representative instance filesystem size (GB) a launch of this model receives — the platform default where the upstream honors a configured size, otherwise the machine's reported disk; varies per offering — see cpu_cores. 0 marks an unreported disk (unknown, not zero). GET /v1/pricing carries the exact per-offering value.

ram_gb.description: Representative host RAM (GB) for this GPU model; varies per offering — see cpu_cores. 0 marks an unreported spec.

storage_gb.description: Representative host storage (GB) for this GPU model; varies per offering — see cpu_cores. 0 marks an unreported spec.

GpuSuggestion.description: Whether a lower-priced GPU model would have fit an instance's observed peak GPU memory. It names GPU models and prices only.

observed_minutes.description: Minutes between the first and the latest telemetry sample.

peak_used_mb.description: Highest GPU memory seen, in MiB. Null with no telemetry.

required_mb.description: The peak plus headroom (25% and 1024 MiB), in MiB: the memory a suggested model must have. Null until there is enough telemetry.

status.description: `suggestion` when a cheaper model fits and the saving is at least 10% and $0.05 per hour. `insufficient_data` until the instance has at least 30 samples over at least an hour. `no_cheaper_fit` otherwise.

GpuSuggestionCheaper.description: The suggested GPU model and what it would save.

price_per_hour.description: The cheapest current listing for this model, per hour.

saving_pct.description: The saving as a percentage of the instance's hourly price.

saving_per_hour.description: The instance's hourly price minus this model's.

GpuSuggestionGpu.description: A GPU model at an hourly price.

gpu_type.description: The GPU model id, as in GET /v1/gpu-types.

price_per_hour.description: Hourly price for the same number of GPUs as the instance.

model.description: Customer-facing image model id (e.g. gpuai/flux.1-schnell) or alias.

n.description: Number of images to generate. Defaults to 1.

prompt.description: Text description of the image(s) to generate.

response_format.description: Only b64_json is supported. A value of "url" is rejected with invalid_request_error until S3-backed URL delivery lands.

created.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the response was created.

image_count.description: Number of images generated (the billable unit).

version.description: Resolved build version; absent for unpinned components (e.g. git).

auto_terminate_at.description: When the runtime limit expires and the platform terminates this instance. Computed when the instance became running (ready_at + auto_terminate_hours), so the countdown covers usable runtime, not the time spent provisioning. Absent when no limit was set, when the instance is not running yet, or once the platform has begun acting on an elapsed limit.

auto_terminate_hours.description: The runtime limit this instance was launched with, in hours (the `auto_terminate_hours` you sent). Absent means the instance runs until something stops it. It stays present after the limit has fired, so a terminated instance still explains itself.

boot_phase.description: How far a launch that is not ready yet has got. machine_requested means the machine was requested and no image download has been reported yet; pulling_image means the image is downloading or unpacking; setting_up means the container is up and the platform is finishing SSH and the GPU check. Present only while status is allocating or starting and the platform is following the boot; absent otherwise. Lets a client with a fixed timeout tell a launch that is still moving from one that is stuck.

app_password.description: HTTP Basic Auth password for app_url and terminal_url. Treat as a secret. OMITTED by default from all reads — returned only on GET /instances/{id}?include=credentials (same persistence availability as app_user); the list endpoint and operation results never include it.

app_url.description: HTTPS URL of the deployed application (template instances only), e.g. https://gpu-abcd1234.apps.gpu.ai.

app_user.description: HTTP Basic Auth username for app_url and terminal_url. Present on instances provisioned after the credential-persistence change; older deploys omit it (their credential was only surfaced once at deploy time).

terminal_url.description: HTTPS URL of the browser web console (a shell on the instance, no SSH key required), e.g. https://gpu-abcd1234-term.apps.gpu.ai. Guarded by the same app_user/app_password login. Present only on running instances provisioned with the console.

disk_gb.description: Instance filesystem size in GB that the platform configured for this launch. Present only where the placed capacity honors a configured disk size; absent means the machine's disk is provider-determined (its own flavor volume).

image.description: The customer-supplied container image this instance was launched from, digest-pinned at verification time (e.g. `ghcr.io/acme/trainer:v1@sha256:…`). Present only on custom-image launches; template and certified launches never expose their images here.

last_reachable_at.description: Last time the platform verified the SSH path to this instance end-to-end through the tunnel. Absent means the instance has not been probed yet (freshly launched, or no tunnel) — it does NOT mean unreachable. An instance whose status is still "running" while this timestamp stops advancing is one whose SSH has died even though the machine is up.

price_per_hour.description: hourly rate for the whole instance — covers all gpu_count GPUs

status.description: Customer-facing lifecycle status. "allocating" = the GPU is still being acquired from the provider (slow-boot capacity such as baremetal can take ~15 min); "starting" = the node exists and is booting; "running" = ready to use. "unreachable" = the platform's tunnel probe has confirmed the SSH path is down while the machine may still be up: the instance is NOT usable right now, billing for the confirmed-dead window is auto-credited back, and the instance either recovers to "running" on its own or is failed after a grace window. It is a degraded reading of a running instance, not a separate lifecycle state — see unreachable_since.

status_reason.description: Why the instance stopped or failed, e.g. "provisioning stalled: the instance started but never became reachable", or — when a runtime limit fired — "Terminated: this instance reached the 8-hour runtime limit set at launch". Present only when the platform has something to explain.

tier.description: `spot` is soft-deprecated: spot capacity is currently unavailable sitewide (requests with tier=spot return no offerings); use on_demand.

unreachable_since.description: Start of the confirmed tunnel outage the instance is currently in. Present exactly when status is "unreachable", absent otherwise. It is the timestamp the auto-credit for the dead window is computed from, so a ledger credit can be reconciled against it.

InstanceDedicatedIP.description: The instance's dedicated public IPv4 add-on. Present only on instances launched with `dedicated_ip`, and only on deployments where the add-on is enabled.

address.description: The GPU.ai-owned public IPv4 address. Point your DNS A record here.

charged_usd.description: Total charged for this address so far (hourly fee plus transfer), in USD.

hourly_fee.description: USD per hour charged while the address is attached, locked at launch.

ports.description: Inbound TCP ports forwarded to the same port on the instance's loopback.

status.description: active means traffic is forwarded. suspended means forwarding has stopped (see suspend_reason), for example after the transfer cap was reached. released means the address was returned because the instance terminated or failed.

suspend_reason.description: Why forwarding is suspended, e.g. `transfer_cap`. Present only while suspended.

transfer_gb.description: GB transferred through the address so far, both directions.

transfer_price_per_gb.description: USD per GB of traffic through the address, both directions, locked at launch.

InstanceGpuMemory.description: The highest GPU memory use seen on an instance since launch, from the telemetry every instance reports about every two minutes. On an instance with several GPUs it is the busiest GPU. Absent on an instance until its first sample arrives.

peak_used_mb.description: Highest memory in use on the GPU, in MiB.

samples.description: How many telemetry samples the peak is taken from.

total_mb.description: The GPU's total memory, in MiB.

issued_at.description: The payment date, which is also the invoice date.

Job.description: A batch job. It names no machine: the machines a job runs on are instances of your organization and appear in the instance list.

attempt.description: The number of the current or last attempt. 0 before the job is first placed.

attempts.description: The job's attempts, oldest first. Returned by GET /v1/jobs/{id} only.

attributed_cost_usd.description: The job's share of its machines' price, for display. A GPU's hourly price is split equally between the jobs running on it at the time, so a job that shared a GPU is attributed less than one that had it alone. A job in a GPU slice is attributed its slice's share of the GPU (for example 3/7 for `3g.40gb`). Machine time with no job running is not attributed to any job. The bill of record is the machine's instance billing.

busy_pct.description: Share of the last finished attempt's samples with GPU utilization at or above 50%. Close to `util_mean_pct` for a job that runs in on/off bursts, near 0 or 100 for a steady one.

cancel_requested.description: True once a cancel has been asked for and until the job stops.

compute_prediction_source.description: Where the compute duty came from: `hint`, `history:org+name`, `history:org+image`, `history:image` or `none` (unknown, counted as 100).

env_names.description: The names of the job's environment variables. Values are never returned.

evictions.description: Times the job was stopped for outgrowing its reservation on a full GPU.

gpu_memory_total_mb.description: Total memory of the GPU the current or last attempt runs on, in MiB.

gpu_seconds.description: Seconds the job has spent running on a GPU, across attempts.

gpu_type.description: The requested GPU model, or an empty string when the job asked for `min_vram_gb` only.

memory_source.description: Where the job's memory numbers come from: `process` is the GPU's per-process accounting, `limit` means per-process memory was not visible and the reservation stands in for it.

mig_profile.description: The GPU slice (NVIDIA MIG profile) a job with `isolation` `hard` runs in during its current or last attempt, such as `3g.40gb`; null for a soft job or one with a whole GPU.

oom_exits.description: Times the job exited out of GPU memory.

peak_memory_mb.description: The job's highest GPU memory use so far, across attempts, in MiB.

predicted_compute_pct.description: The compute duty the current or last attempt was charged on its GPU, 1 to 100. 100 when the job's compute is unknown.

predicted_mb.description: The estimate behind the reservation, from the hint or from history, with headroom.

prediction_source.description: Where the reservation came from: `hint`, `history:org+name`, `history:org+image`, `history:image`, `none` (no hint and no usable history), `not_shared` (the job did not opt in to sharing) or `no_restart` (sharing needs restart). `+retry` is appended once a memory failure has grown the reservation.

reservation_mb.description: GPU memory reserved for the current or last attempt, in MiB. For a whole GPU it is the GPU's total memory. It is used for placement and is not a hard cap.

retries.description: Reruns after a memory failure, counted against `max_retries`.

secrets.description: Names of the organization secrets the job receives. Empty when none.

sharing_mode.description: How the GPU was shared during the last attempt. `mig` is a GPU slice of the job's own.

started_at.description: When the current or last attempt started.

status.description: `queued` is waiting for a GPU, `assigned` has a GPU and is about to start, `running` is running. `succeeded`, `failed` and `cancelled` are final. A job that is retried goes back to `queued`.

status_reason.description: Why the job is waiting, or why it failed or was retried.

trial_funded.description: The job was submitted with no balance and runs on the free trial. It stops when the trial credit is used.

util_mean_pct.description: Mean GPU utilization measured during the last finished attempt. See `compute_source` on the attempt for how it was attributed.

wait_for_capacity.description: The job was submitted with `wait_for_capacity`: it waits for a machine of its type for up to 24 hours instead of being refused or failed for lack of capacity.

whole_gpu.description: Whether the current or last attempt has a GPU to itself. Null before the job is first placed.

compute_source.description: How the attempt's compute profile was attributed. `process` is the job's own per-process utilization, measured even while it shared. `solo` uses the GPU's utilization while the job was alone on it. `shared_upper_bound` uses the GPU's utilization while it shared, which over-states the job's own.

mig_profile.description: The GPU slice the attempt ran in, or null.

outcome.description: How the attempt ended. `oom` is an out-of-memory exit, `evicted` is a stop for outgrowing the reservation on a full GPU, `lost` means the machine or the container disappeared, and `infra` means the GPU's sharing layer failed under the job. `lost` and `infra` do not use a retry. Null while the attempt is in progress.

resumed.description: Whether the attempt started with files already in its checkpoint directory.

allow_restart.description: Opt in to restart. The platform may stop the job and run it again: after it runs out of GPU memory, after it outgrows its reservation on a full GPU, or after its machine is lost. Use the checkpoint directory to resume instead of starting over.

allow_sharing.description: Opt in to sharing. The job may run on the same GPU as other jobs from your own organization that also opted in. Needs `allow_restart`, and a memory hint or usable history; otherwise the job still gets a whole GPU. A GPU is never shared with another customer.

checkpoint_path.description: Where the job's checkpoint directory is mounted inside the container. Defaults to `/gpuai/checkpoint`. The same path is in the `GPUAI_CHECKPOINT_DIR` environment variable. Files written there are still present when the job is run again on the same machine. They do not follow the job to another machine.

command.description: The program and its arguments. The first item replaces the image's entrypoint and the rest are its arguments, so `["python", "train.py", "--epochs", "3"]` runs exactly that. Send this or `script`.

compute_hint_pct.description: The share of time you expect the job to keep the GPU busy, 1 to 100. Jobs share a GPU only while the sum of their compute duties stays at or under 100. Without a hint the platform uses the measured utilization of earlier finished jobs with the same name or image, and a job with neither counts as 100 (a GPU to itself).

env.description: Environment variables for the job, at most 100. Names starting with `GPUAI_` are reserved. Values are stored to run the job and are never returned by the API.

env_from_job.description: The id of an earlier job of yours whose environment variables this job starts with. Variables in `env` are applied over them. Use it to resubmit an edited job without sending its values again: the API never returns env values. Returns 422 `validation_failed` when no such job of your organization exists.

gpu_type.description: The GPU model to run on, as in GET /v1/gpu-types. One of `gpu_type` or `min_vram_gb` is required.

image.description: The container image to run, such as `registry.example.com/team/train:1.2`. The machine must be able to pull it without credentials. Required unless the deployment runs a default image: then it may be left out, `gpu_type` is required, and the job runs on the GPU.ai PyTorch image built for that GPU.

input_file.description: The id of a file uploaded with POST /jobs/inputs. When the job starts it gets a short-lived URL of the file in `GPUAI_INPUT_URL` and its name in `GPUAI_INPUT_NAME`. A file is read by one job only. Returns 422 `validation_failed` when the file was not uploaded, has expired, is already used, or job files are not enabled on this deployment.

isolation.description: `soft` (the default) is the sharing described under `allow_sharing`. `hard` runs the job in a GPU slice of its own (NVIDIA MIG): its own memory, its own compute and its own fault domain, so another job on the same GPU cannot slow it down, take its memory or crash it. The slice is the smallest that holds the memory hint or the job's history; without either, or when no slice is large enough, the job gets a whole GPU. A slice has a share of the GPU's compute in proportion to its size, so a job in a small slice runs slower than on a whole GPU. Needs `gpu_type` set to a model that supports slices (`a100_80gb` or `h100_pcie`), and cannot be combined with `allow_sharing`. Not available until enabled for your organization.

max_price_per_hour.description: Only run on a machine whose hourly price is at most this. Machines are launched on the cheapest suitable listing in any region.

max_retries.description: How many times to rerun the job after it runs out of GPU memory or is stopped for outgrowing its reservation. Defaults to 2. Other failures are never retried.

max_wait_seconds.description: Opt in to waiting. When no machine in your pool has room, wait up to this long for space before starting a new machine. 0 starts a machine at once.

memory_hint_mb.description: The peak GPU memory you expect the job to use, in MiB. The reservation is the hint plus headroom (15% and 512 MiB). Without a hint the platform uses the history of earlier finished jobs, and a job with neither gets a whole GPU.

min_vram_gb.description: Run on any GPU model with at least this much memory, in GB. Used when `gpu_type` is not given.

name.description: A label for the job. Jobs whose names match once digits are removed (`train-run-17`, `train-run-18`) are treated as repeats of the same work, and the peak memory of earlier finished runs is used to size later ones. Naming repeat jobs consistently is the simplest way to have them share a GPU without a memory hint.

repo.description: A git repository cloned into `/workspace/repo`, the working directory of the command or script. Only where the deployment runs a default image. For a private repository, store a token as the organization secret `GIT_TOKEN` and name it in `secrets`.

ref.description: A branch, tag or commit. Empty means the default branch.

url.description: An https URL of the repository, with no credentials in it.

script.description: A shell script run with `bash -c` in place of `command`, such as `pip install -r requirements.txt && python train.py`. Only where the deployment runs a default image; elsewhere it is refused with a 422.

secrets.description: Names of organization secrets (POST /secrets) the job's container receives as environment variables of the same names. Values are never in a response or a log. Returns 422 `validation_failed` when a name does not exist or secrets are not enabled on this deployment.

timeout_seconds.description: The job is stopped and fails after running this long.

wait_for_capacity.description: Queue the job even when no machine of its GPU type is available right now (`available_now` false in `GET /jobs/gpu-types`), and keep it waiting for one for up to 24 hours. Without it such a job is refused with 422 and the nearest type that is available, and a queued job whose machine launches keep being refused for lack of capacity fails within a few minutes.

capacity_checked.description: True when `available_now` is a live answer that submit acts on: a job for a type that is not available now (or, with only `min_vram_gb`, when no available type is that large) is refused with 422 unless it sets `wait_for_capacity`. False when the stock could not be read just now: nothing is then refused for capacity.

complete.description: True when the list is authoritative and any other gpu_type is refused at submit.

available_now.description: True when a supplier that runs jobs had a one-GPU machine of this type to rent at the last catalog read, a few minutes ago, and recent launches of it were not refused. When `capacity_checked` is true, a job for a type that is not available now is refused unless it sets `wait_for_capacity`.

last_seen_at.description: When a supplier that runs jobs last listed the type.

price_per_gpu_hour.description: Cheapest retail price in USD per GPU-hour of such a machine at that read. Null when not available now.

expires_at.description: When the file is deleted if no job has read it.

upload_url.description: PUT the file's bytes here in one request.

bytes.description: The file's exact size in bytes.

filename.description: The file's name. Reduced to letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore.

text.description: A piece of the job's combined output, at most 16 KB.

next_after.description: Pass this as `after` to read on from here.

files.description: The files in the archive, at most 200 listed.

max_bytes.description: The most one job's outputs may hold.

message.description: What the status means for this job, in plain words.

outputs_path.description: The directory in the container that is uploaded.

url.description: Downloads the zip archive until url_expires_at.

JobSharingHint.description: Advisory only, and present only when it applies. A job carries it when it succeeded with a whole GPU it did not allow to be shared, ran at least a minute with no out-of-memory exit or eviction, and its peak GPU memory, measured from per-process accounting (`memory_source` `process`), was at most half of the GPU's memory. Sharing stays opt-in; the hint never changes how a job is placed.

gpu_memory_total_mb.description: Total memory of the GPU the job held, in MiB.

message.description: A short sentence to show the user, such as "This job used 5.1 GB of its 48 GB GPU. Set allow_sharing and allow_restart to true to let it share a GPU with your other jobs and pay only for its share." It names only the flags the job did not already set.

peak_memory_mb.description: The job's measured peak GPU memory, in MiB.

gpu_memory_mb.description: Memory in use on the whole GPU, all jobs included, in MiB.

gpu_util_pct.description: Utilization of the whole GPU, in percent.

memory_mb.description: The job's highest GPU memory use in the window, in MiB.

cap_cents.description: The most the trial credits one organization, in cents.

credited_cents.description: Trial credit added to the balance so far, in cents.

eligible.description: True while this organization's jobs are credited back as they run.

enabled.description: False when this deployment runs no trial. Every other field is then zero.

funding.description: How an eligible organization's trial is paid for. `credit_back`: it pays as usual and job cost is credited back. `no_deposit`: it has no balance and may submit a trial job now. `deposit_first`: it has no balance and must add credits first. Omitted when not eligible.

max_price_per_hour.description: The most a trial job's GPU may cost per hour. Only with `funding` no_deposit, and only when the deployment sets such a limit (by default it sets none).

max_runtime_seconds.description: The longest a trial job may run. Only with `funding` no_deposit, and only when the deployment sets such a limit (by default it sets none).

message.description: The line to show the user, e.g. "Your first jobs are free, up to $10." Omitted when not eligible.

reason.description: Why the organization is not eligible. Omitted when eligible.

remaining_cents.description: How much more job cost the trial covers, in cents.

MarketHistoryPoint.description:
One bucket of a price/stock series.

The nullability of `price_per_gpu_hour` and `available_count` is the contract, not a convenience: a real 0 is a bucket we sampled and found sold out, and null is a bucket we never successfully sampled. A client that coerces null to 0 will report GPU.ai's own polling outages as supplier stockouts, and must not interpolate across a null.

available_count.description: Obtainable units across every matching offer in this bucket. 0 means we sampled and the market was sold out; null means we did not sample this bucket.

bucket_ts.description: Start of the bucket, UTC, aligned to the bucket width.

gpu_count.description: GPUs in that node. Present only alongside `node_price_per_hour`, and it is what lets a renderer qualify a derived rate as "(from an 8-GPU node)" rather than implying single-GPU rentability.

node_price_per_hour.description: Whole-node hourly price the per-GPU rate was divided out of. Present only when the bucket's floor came from a multi-GPU node; absent for single-GPU capacity.

price_per_gpu_hour.description: GPU.ai's floor per-GPU hourly rate for this bucket, or null if we did not sample this bucket. Null is NOT zero.

MarketHistoryResponse.description:
A price/stock series for one (gpu_model, region, capacity_class) key.

Points cover the FULL bucket grid across the requested window, including the buckets we did not sample — a gap therefore has visible width rather than disappearing between two adjacent points.

available_cluster_sizes.description:
The node shapes that actually have rows in this window, for this gpu_model / region / capacity_class — what a size picker may honestly offer.

This is what we SAMPLED, not what we may ever sell: offering a shape a model was never listed at draws an empty chart a caller reads as a stockout. An empty array means we looked and found none. It is unaffected by the cluster_size parameter, so a picker's options never depend on which option is currently selected.

bucket_seconds.description: Resolution the server actually answered at. Echoed because the wide views downsample at query time, so a client must never assume 900.

capacity_class.description: Echoes the request. Empty means the series is merged across both classes.

cluster_size.description: Echoes the request. 0 means the series is MERGED across every node shape, the same thing an omitted parameter meant on the way in.

region.description: Echoes the request. Empty means the series is MERGED across every region, the same thing it meant on the way in.

fine_tunable.description: Whether this model can be used as the base of a managed fine-tuning job. The tunable allowlist is operator-curated and much narrower than the serving catalog, so this is false for almost every model. Absent means false.

fine_tune_base_model.description: The exact id to send as `model` when creating a fine-tuning job for this entry. Present only when `fine_tunable` is true, and deliberately distinct from `id`: the allowlist matches the customer-facing base id (e.g. `qwen2.5-7b-instruct`), which a served model normally carries as an alias rather than as its namespaced catalog id.

parameters.description: Typed parameter descriptors for media (image/video) models — name, type, enum/bounds/default. Playgrounds render input forms from these.

default.description: Default value for the field (any JSON scalar).

cached_input_per_1m_tokens_cents.description: cached_input_per_1m_tokens_microcents rounded to whole cents; omitted when the exact rate rounds below half a cent.

cached_input_per_1m_tokens_microcents.description: Exact per-1M-token rate in micro-cents (1e-6 cent) for the cache-HIT part of a chat prompt (usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens). Present only on models with a published cached-input rate; absent means no discount — every prompt token bills at input_per_1m_tokens_cents. Treat this field as the presence signal: cached rates are routinely sub-cent, so the rounded cents field below is often omitted.

peak_windows_utc.description: The daily UTC ranges during which the `peak` rates apply, start inclusive and end exclusive ("24:00" is a valid end; a range whose end sorts before its start wraps midnight). Present only on a model priced by time of day.

per_image_microcents.description: Exact per-image rate in micro-cents (1e-6 cent). Prefer this for image models — per_image_cents rounds sub-cent prices to 0.

per_mpxl_microcents.description: Price per output megapixel in micro-cents (1e-6 cent) for image models metered per megapixel. Mutually exclusive with the per-image fields.

per_video_microcents.description: Representative per-clip price in micro-cents (1e-6 cent) for video models — a "from" price taken from the provider's published example rate.

per_video_second_microcents.description: Exact per-second-of-output-video rate in micro-cents (1e-6 cent). Prefer this for video models.

period.description: Present only on a model priced by time of day. Which side of the peak schedule the instant this response was rendered falls on; the flat rate fields above are the rates in effect at that instant. A request is billed at the rate in effect when it ARRIVES (UTC), so a caller planning a call for later should price it from `peak` / `off_peak` and `peak_windows_utc`.

supports_structured_outputs.description: Chat models only. True when POST /v1/chat/completions accepts response_format json_object / json_schema for this model and tier.

supports_tools.description: Chat models only. True when POST /v1/chat/completions accepts tools / tool_choice / parallel_tool_calls for this model and tier.

zero_data_retention.description: True when this model and tier can be served with zero data retention: at least one model host keeps no prompt or output content. Only these models are callable by an org with zero data retention on, or with the X-GPUAI-Zero-Data-Retention header. Always false for video.

ModelRate.description: One per-1M-token rate triple, in rounded cents and exact micro-cents (1e-6 cent). Prefer the micro-cent fields for arithmetic; cached rates are routinely sub-cent and their cents field is then omitted.

OfferingAlternative.description: A live catalog row a launch whose pinned offering was gone could take instead. Same fields and meaning as the matching GET /pricing row.

type.description: OpenAI error class (e.g. invalid_request_error, authentication_error, billing_error).

alternatives.description: Present only when code is offering_unavailable: up to three live catalog rows of the same GPU type, count and tier, cheapest first. Pass one's offering_id as the new pin.

code.description: Stable machine-readable failure code (see Problem.code), for example operation_failed (retryable after a backoff), price_changed or offering_unavailable (not retryable as sent).

current_price_per_hour.description: Present only when code is price_changed: the live hourly price the launch found.

max_price_per_hour.description: Present only when code is price_changed: the hourly price the launch was approved at (max_price_per_hour, or the viewed price). Relaunch with max_price_per_hour of at least current_price_per_hour to accept the new price.

hint.description: Advisory pointer to Jobs (POST /jobs), present only on the synchronous 202 from POST /instances and only on some launches: when the request is a one-off batch run, or the organization launched many instances in the last 24 hours that each ran for less than 15 minutes. Same text as the GPUAI-Hint header. Never on GET /operations/{id} polls, and it never changes the launch.

result.description: Terminal-success payload. Carries the per-instance web-access coordinates — app_url for template deploys, terminal_url for instances provisioned with the browser web console, and the basic-auth username shared by both. The basic-auth PASSWORD is never included here — retrieve it via GET /instances/{id}?include=credentials (connection.app_password).

warnings.description: Create-time advisories, present only on the synchronous 202 from POST /instances (never on GET /operations/{id} polls) — e.g. the model-size guard failing open because a template deploy's MODEL is a gated or unknown Hugging Face repo whose size could not be verified.

PeakWindow.description: One daily UTC time range during which a model's peak rates apply.

available.description: count of available units, summed across merged identical offers

capacity_class.description: per-offering capacity classification — "secure" for datacenter-operated hardware, "community" for supplier/peer-hosted hardware with a softer SLA. The string twin of `community`, classified per offering rather than per upstream. May transiently be empty for cache entries written before the field existed.

community.description: true when this offering is community-supplied capacity

cpu_cores.description: host vCPU count for this offering, tied to the shown (cheapest) price. 0 marks an unreported spec.

disk_configurable.description: true when a launch of this offering may choose its own disk size via the create request's disk_gb. A distinguishing field in the offer merge — configurable and fixed-disk capacity for the same SKU stay separate rows.

disk_price_per_gb_hour.description: Retail price of one GB of instance disk beyond instance_disk_gb, per hour, for launches of this offering. A launch requesting disk_gb above instance_disk_gb is billed approximately price_per_hour + (disk_gb − instance_disk_gb) × disk_price_per_gb_hour (the exact billed rate folds disk into one cent-rounded hourly price). 0 when the offering is not disk-configurable, or when disk above the included allowance is currently free.

gpu_count.description: number of GPUs in the listed configuration

instance_disk_gb.description: Instance filesystem size (GB) a launch of THIS offering receives — the platform default where the upstream honors a configured size, otherwise the machine's own reported disk; tied to the shown (cheapest) price like cpu_cores. 0 marks an unreported disk (unknown, not zero).

instant_boot.description: true when instances of this offering are typically reachable within about a minute of launch; false for capacity with longer provisioning times (~3-5 minutes)

price_per_hour.description: hourly price for the whole listed configuration — covers all gpu_count GPUs

ram_gb.description: host RAM (GB) for this offering, tied to the shown price. 0 marks an unreported spec.

storage_gb.description: host storage (GB) for this offering, tied to the shown price. 0 marks an unreported spec.

tier.description: `spot` is soft-deprecated: spot capacity is currently unavailable sitewide (requests with tier=spot return no offerings); use on_demand.

RegisterCommunityMachineRequest.description: All fields optional; an empty body registers a zero-spec placeholder in pending_verification.

tier.description: Supplier-chosen rental model. Optional; omitted resolves to on_demand. spot lists the machine as cheaper interruptible capacity.

RegistryCredential.description: A stored private-registry login (metadata only — the password is write-only and encrypted at rest).

SavedCard.description: A saved card. Brand, last 4 digits and expiry only; never a card number.

is_default.description: The card auto-pay and an unqualified card top-up charge.

Secret.description: An organization secret's metadata. There is no value field: values are write-only and never returned.

last_used_at.description: When the value was last delivered to a machine, or null.

name.description: The secret's name, which is also the environment variable it is delivered as.

version.description: How many times the value has been written. Starts at 1.

value.description: The secret value. Write-only; never returned.

overwrite.description: Replace the values of secrets that already exist. False leaves them untouched.

skipped.description: Names that already existed and were left untouched (overwrite false).

description.description: Omit to keep the current description.

value.description: The secret value. Write-only; never returned.

include_usage.description: When true, the final stream chunk carries usage totals (CHAT-03).

SupplierMachineView.description: The supplier-facing projection of a community machine. `occupied` replaces the renting customer's instance id (never exposed to the supplier); `online` is the server-derived 60s-heartbeat liveness.

occupied.description: A customer instance is currently renting this machine.

online.description: Server-derived — heartbeated within the last 60 seconds.

reliability_score.description: Server-computed 0–100; machines below the platform threshold are auto-delisted.

Template.description: A deployable application template. The container image (registry path) and start command are internal orchestration details and are intentionally absent from this schema (TMPL-13 defense-by-omission).

kind.description: Deployable kind. "service" is a long-running app exposed at connection.app_url. "finetuning" is a run-to-completion job (no app_url) and is currently advertised only as a coming-soon catalog entry — not yet deployable.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code; empty clears it.

tax_id.description: Write only. Stored encrypted and never returned in full. Empty removes the stored Tax ID.

price_per_hour.description: Whole-machine hourly rate (never per-GPU). Must clear the platform floor; a below-floor price is rejected with `price-below-floor` carrying the concrete `floor_per_hour`.

driver_preinstalled.description: true when the image ships the NVIDIA driver + CUDA baked in.

model.description: Customer-facing video model id (e.g. gpuai/wan-2.2-t2v) or alias.

prompt.description: Text description of the video to generate.

seconds.description: Output video duration in seconds (the billable unit).

completed_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the job completed.

cost_cents.description: Final billed cost in cents; present once the job completes (failed/cancelled jobs are never billed).

created_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the job was created.

error.description: Canonical failure code when status is failed.

expires_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the artifact expires (24h after completion).

WatchRule.description: A rule that notifies when the market moves on a GPU model. It carries no upstream supplier identity of any kind, and no delivery address — those are properties of the resource, not of a particular response.

capacity_class.description: Capacity class the rule is narrowed to, or null for both.

deactivated_reason.description: Why an automatically disabled rule was disabled — for example its creator no longer belongs to the organization.

gpu_model.description: The canonical GPU model id the rule watches, e.g. "h100_sxm" — a MODEL, not a generation. Alerts match the live catalog exactly, so a rule for a model we do not list could never fire and is refused rather than stored. Case and punctuation are forgiving ("H100-SXM" resolves to "h100_sxm"), and the canonical id is what is stored and returned. GET /v1/gpu-types lists the models currently on offer; a model with no stock right now is still watchable, which is the point of watching it.

quiet_until.description: While set, the rule will not re-fire even if the condition re-crosses — the quiet window that stops a boundary-hugging signal alerting on every crossing.

region.description: Canonical region the rule is narrowed to, or null for every region.

state.description: armed = the condition is currently false and the next transition to true will alert. fired = it has alerted and has not yet re-armed.

threshold.description: Per-GPU hourly price for price_under, or a unit count for count_at_least. Null for in_stock, which takes no threshold.

webhook_endpoint_override_id.description: Id of a webhook endpoint registered by this organization, or null to deliver to every registered endpoint. Never a URL.

capacity_class.description: Omit or send null to watch both capacity classes.

enabled.description: Defaults to true. Create with false to park a rule.

gpu_model.description: The canonical GPU model id the rule watches, e.g. "h100_sxm" — a MODEL, not a generation. Alerts match the live catalog exactly, so a rule for a model we do not list could never fire and is refused rather than stored. Case and punctuation are forgiving ("H100-SXM" resolves to "h100_sxm"), and the canonical id is what is stored and returned. GET /v1/gpu-types lists the models currently on offer; a model with no stock right now is still watchable, which is the point of watching it.

region.description: Omit or send null to watch every region.

threshold.description: Required and greater than zero for price_under and count_at_least. Ignored for in_stock, which is stored with no threshold.

webhook_endpoint_override_id.description: Id of an endpoint already registered via /webhook-endpoints. A URL here is rejected: the resource holds references, never addresses.

WatchRuleUpdate.description: Partial update. An absent key keeps the stored value; an explicit null on region, capacity_class or webhook_endpoint_override_id clears it. The merged rule is re-validated as a whole.

secret.description: Returned ONLY at creation; subsequent reads omit.

folder_bytes.description: Size of the workspace folder now.

price_per_hour.description: GPU price of the current machine (0 when stopped).

url.description: The IDE's address; open it with a link from /workspaces/{id}/open.

idle_timeout.description: Seconds without use before the workspace saves and stops.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter (32 at most).

offering_id.description: Place the machine on this offering, as on instance create.

port.description: Open a private app link to this port; omit for the IDE.

gpu_type.description: Another GPU type to start on (switch GPU).

max_price_per_hour.description: Highest hourly GPU price, USD; null removes it. Kept for later starts; raise it to start on a pricier GPU.

app.description: The web app the template runs (ComfyUI), opened as a private app link on its port.

max_price_per_hour.description: Highest hourly GPU price, USD; null removes it. Applies from the next start.

info.description:
Programmatic API for GPU.ai. Authenticate with API keys minted from
the dashboard. See https://gpu.ai/docs for details.
info.title: GPU.ai Public Developer API

get.description: Lists this organization's auto-launch rules. Requires the `autolaunch:read` scope, which `standard` and `full_access` keys carry. Rules belonging to other organizations are never returned, and rules created through the dashboard are included — the list is the organization's, not the key's.

post.description:
Creates a standing, pre-approved purchase order. When the condition holds and the live price is at or under `max_price_per_hour`, the platform launches the frozen `spec` with no further confirmation from anyone — the customer is approving NOW for a purchase that happens LATER, while nobody is watching.

SCOPE. Requires the `autolaunch:write` scope, which is granted only EXPLICITLY. It is deliberately NOT covered by `full_access`, `standard` or `read_only`: `instances:write` is real-time authority, exercised with someone present, whereas this is a standing, frozen authorization that fires days later unattended. Treating them as the same authority class would have handed unattended spend authority to every key ever issued, including keys minted long before this resource existed. Most existing keys therefore receive 403 here; the correct response is to mint a key whose scopes map includes `{"autolaunch": "write"}`, never to retry, to substitute a key, or to fall back to a watch rule.

CONSENT. `acknowledged_max_total_usd` is REQUIRED and must equal `max_price_per_hour × max_runtime_hours` to within one cent. It is the API-level expression of "a valid confirmation must come AFTER the price": a caller that never computed the number cannot have shown it to anyone, and a caller that displayed a different number disagrees with what is about to be stored. Show the figure to the person approving the rule, then send it back.

TWO PRICES, TWO UNITS. `threshold` is the TRIGGER, in dollars per GPU-hour — the same unit the market chart and watch rules speak in. `max_price_per_hour` is the CEILING, in dollars per hour for the WHOLE instance.
