A 4-GPU rule triggering under $4.00/GPU-hr typically carries a $16.00/hr ceiling. Conflating them scales the customer's spend authorization by their GPU count.

FROZEN SPEC. `spec` is the full create-instance body the rule replays, validated at creation with the same validation a live create runs, so a spec that could never launch is refused while a human is present rather than at 3 a.m. `spec.offering_id` is REJECTED — offering identity churns between catalog polls, so a pin produces a rule that can never fire, which is the worst outcome here because the customer believes a purchase is armed. `spec.auto_terminate_hours` is overwritten from `max_runtime_hours` and must not be used to widen the bound.

Organizations are limited to 10 active rules; the 422 names the limit. The organization spending limit still applies as a backstop at fire time — a launch must fit both its own ceiling and the org cap.

403.description: The API key lacks `autolaunch:write`. This scope is explicit-grant only and is NOT covered by `full_access`, `standard` or `read_only`; the problem detail names the scope and the fix.

422.description:
Validation failed — a missing or mismatched `acknowledged_max_total_usd`, a missing ceiling or runtime bound, an unknown condition kind, a non-canonical region, a missing threshold on a threshold condition, a `spec` that would not launch, a pinned `spec.offering_id`, or the active-rule limit already reached.

Also refused: anything that would arm a rule which can never succeed. A `gpu_model` (or `spec.gpu_type`) that is not a model we list; a `spec.gpu_type` that disagrees with the rule's `gpu_model`; and a `spec.gpu_count` that is not a node shape a single launch can ask for (1, 2, 4 or 8 — 3, 5, 6 and 7 all pass an ordinary bounds check and none is a machine anyone rents).

NOT refused: a `max_price_per_hour` below `threshold` x `spec.gpu_count`. The two are in different units — `threshold` is per GPU-hour, the ceiling is for the WHOLE instance — but the launch aborts only above ceiling/gpu_count, a LOWER bar than the trigger, so such a rule waits and then buys once the market falls far enough. That shape is supported deliberately.

post.summary: Create an auto-launch rule (pre-approves a bounded, unattended spend)

delete.description: Deletes the rule and withdraws its pre-approved spend cap immediately. Requires only the `autolaunch:read` scope, for the same reason the disarm PATCH does. Deleting an already-deleted rule returns 404.

get.description: Fetches one auto-launch rule, including the frozen launch spec. Requires the `autolaunch:read` scope. A rule belonging to another organization returns 404 — the same answer as an id that does not exist.

patch.description:
Disarms a rule. The body must be exactly `{"enabled": false}` and nothing else. Requires only the `autolaunch:read` scope — cancelling a standing spend authorization is deliberately never harder than holding one, so a key narrowed since it created a rule can still stop that rule.

This is the entire update surface, and the absence is the design. Changing a ceiling, a runtime bound, the targeting or the frozen spec is a DIFFERENT bounded purchase, so it requires deleting the rule and creating a new one through the consent gate. Re-arming is refused too: a fired rule consumed its one shot, so `{"enabled": true}` would resurrect a purchase order that was already consented to and spent.

422.description: The body carried a key other than `enabled`, omitted `enabled`, or asked to re-arm the rule.

get.description:
Returns the organization's credit balance, its auto-pay configuration, and the live burn rate. Requires the `billing:read` scope. The organization is taken from the authenticated API key, never from a parameter.

Divide `balance_cents` by `burn_cents_per_hour` for the remaining runway in hours. The quotient is undefined in three cases a caller must keep apart: `burn_cents_per_hour` is 0 (nothing running, so the balance funds unbounded idle time), it is `null` (the burn rate could not be determined — NOT the same as idle), or the balance is already at or below zero.

This is the balance itself — for spend against a configured cap see `/billing/spending-limit`, and for past consumption see `/usage`.

`runway_hours` does that division for you, adding serverless inference spend over the last hour to the burn. While it is under the low-balance threshold (2 hours by default) and auto-pay is off or failing, every authenticated response carries the `GPUAI-Balance-Warning` header.

Returns the organization's stablecoin deposits, newest first, capped at 50. Requires the `billing:read` scope. The organization is taken from the authenticated API key, never from a parameter. Returns 404 when stablecoin deposits are not enabled for this deployment.

min_deposit_cents.description: The effective minimum deposit in USD cents (admin override, else the deployment's configured floor). Validate amounts against this live value rather than hardcoding the default.

post.description:
Charges one of the organization's saved cards off-session and returns the Stripe PaymentIntent id as `deposit_id`. The balance is credited a few seconds later by GPU.ai's Stripe webhook, exactly like a deposit made on the website, including any deposit-match promotion and its card hold; poll `GET /billing/deposits/card/{id}` to see it land.

Requires the `payments:write` scope, carried by `full_access` keys (what `gpu login` issues to an organization admin) and by an explicit `{"payments": "write"}` grant, never by `standard` or `read_only`. The key owner must also be an organization admin.

Limits (server configuration, defaults shown): at most $10,000 per charge and $25,000 of saved-card charges per organization in any rolling 24 hours (declined or canceled charges do not count, and a charge left waiting for 3-D Secure stops counting after an hour). Saved-card charging can be switched off by an operator; it then answers `503 card-topup-disabled` and `POST /billing/deposits/card/checkout` still works.

An `Idempotency-Key` header is REQUIRED. Retrying with the same key replays the first attempt (here and at Stripe) instead of charging again; use a new key for each deliberate top-up. When the card issuer requires 3-D Secure, the response has `status: requires_action` and an `action_url` to open in a browser.

payment_method_id.description: A saved card id from `GET /billing/payment-methods`. Omit to charge the default card (the one auto-pay uses).

402.description: `card-declined` — the issuer declined; nothing was charged.

403.description: `insufficient_scope` — the key lacks `payments:write`. `forbidden` — not an organization admin. `org-frozen` — the organization cannot add funds.

409.description: `no-saved-card` — no (matching) saved card; use `POST /billing/deposits/card/checkout` once to save one. `idempotency-key-used` — this key belongs to a top-up that already failed.

422.description: `card-topup-limit` — over the per-charge limit. `card-topup-daily-limit` — over the organization's rolling-24h limit; the detail says how much is left.

503.description: `card-topup-disabled` — saved-card charging is switched off; use Checkout.

post.summary: Top up the balance by charging a saved card

post.description: Creates the same Stripe Checkout session as the dashboard's "Add credits" and returns its URL as `checkout_url`. Nothing is charged until the customer pays on that page; paying saves the card for later `POST /billing/deposits/card` top-ups. Requires the `billing:write` scope AND an organization admin. `deposit_id` is the Checkout Session id; poll `GET /billing/deposits/card/{id}`.

403.description: `forbidden` — not an organization admin. `org-frozen` — the organization cannot add funds.

post.summary: Top up the balance with Stripe Checkout

get.description: Reports whether a card top-up has been credited to the balance, and what any deposit-match promotion decided for it. Requires the `billing:read` scope. Reads GPU.ai's ledger, never Stripe: an id that belongs to another organization reads as `pending`.

post.description: Creates a deposit intent and returns the payment address and the exact token amount to send. Requires the `billing:write` scope; any member of the organization may add funds. Send the exact `pay_amount` of `asset` on `chain` and no other network — funds sent on a different network are not detected automatically. Returns 404 when stablecoin deposits are not enabled for this deployment.

amount_cents.description: Amount to deposit in USD cents. Must be at least the configured minimum (500 = $5.00 by default).

400.description: `validation-error` — `amount_cents` is below the configured minimum. `unsupported-chain-asset` — the chain/asset pair is not available. `invalid-request` — malformed JSON body.

403.description: `org-frozen` — the organization cannot add funds; contact support.

503.description: `payment-source-unavailable` — deposits are temporarily unavailable; retry shortly.

get.description: Returns a single deposit belonging to the caller's organization. Requires the `billing:read` scope. A deposit belonging to another organization returns the same `404 deposit-not-found` as one that does not exist — deliberately, so this endpoint cannot be used to test whether a deposit id is real. Also 404 when stablecoin deposits are not enabled for this deployment.

404.description: `deposit-not-found` — no such deposit, or it belongs to another organization. `not-found` — the feature is not enabled.

get.description: Returns the company name, address and Tax ID printed on the organization's invoices. Requires the `billing:read` scope. The Tax ID is stored encrypted and is only ever returned masked (`tax_id_masked`); the full value is printed on the organization's own invoice PDFs and nowhere else.

patch.description: Updates the billing details printed on invoices. Requires the `billing:write` scope and an org admin's key. Omitted fields keep their value. `tax_id` replaces the stored Tax ID (and needs `tax_id_type` unless one is already stored); an empty `tax_id` removes it. Returns 503 `tax-id-unavailable` when this deployment cannot store a Tax ID.

get.description: Returns the organization's invoices, newest first. Every payment (card purchase, auto-pay top up, stablecoin deposit) has one; promotional credit does not. Requires the `billing:read` scope.

Returns one invoice as a PDF, including the organization's billing details and full Tax ID. Requires the `billing:read` scope. An invoice belonging to another organization returns the same 404 as one that does not exist.

Returns the organization's saved cards as brand, last 4 digits and expiry. Card numbers are never returned. Requires the `payments:read` scope AND an organization admin (members get 403). An organization with no saved card returns an empty list. `saved_card_charge_allowed` says whether the calling key may charge these cards (`payments:write`).

daily_cap_cents.description: The per-organization rolling-24h limit on saved-card charges, in cents.

max_charge_cents.description: The per-charge limit for API card top-ups, in cents.

saved_card_charge_allowed.description: True when the calling key holds `payments:write`, i.e. `POST /billing/deposits/card` can succeed for it.

saved_card_charge_enabled.description: False when saved-card charging is switched off right now; use `POST /billing/deposits/card/checkout` instead.

403.description: `forbidden` — the key owner is not an organization admin. `insufficient_scope` — the key lacks `payments:read`.

get.description: Returns the organization's monthly spending limit and opt-in daily spend cap, with the current month and day spend. Requires the `billing:read` scope. Returns 404 when no limit is configured.

put.description: Sets the monthly spending limit and optionally sets or clears the opt-in daily spend cap. Requires the `billing:write` scope AND org-admin privileges (a non-admin member gets 403). `daily_limit_dollars` uses pointer semantics: omit to leave the cap unchanged, 0 to clear it, a positive value to set it.

auto_terminate_hours.description: Hours after the limit is reached before auto-terminate; null = never.

daily_limit_dollars.description: Opt-in daily cap in USD. Omit = unchanged, 0 = clear, > 0 = set.

schema.description: Server-Sent Events stream of ChatCompletionChunk objects, terminated by `data: [DONE]`.

200.description:
Successful response. application/json for non-streaming requests;
text/event-stream for streaming requests (stream=true).

get.description: Lists the organization's clusters (and deleted ones whose machines are still being released) with status, machine counts and cost so far. Requires the `instances:read` scope.

post.description: Creates a cluster of GPU machines joined on an encrypted private network (WireGuard) as one Kubernetes cluster, with Ray (KubeRay) and the KAI scheduler (NVIDIA's open-source Run:ai scheduler) installed. GPU.ai rents `min_nodes` machines right away and adds machines when work waits for GPUs, up to `max_nodes`; a machine with no GPU work for `idle_timeout` seconds is removed, down to `min_nodes`. Each machine is billed like an instance. `placement` "spread" places machines on different suppliers where it can. Returns 422 `validation_failed` for a bad field, 409 `name_taken` for a duplicate name, 409 `limit_reached` at the per-organization cap, and 402 `insufficient_balance` when the prepaid balance is not positive (a cluster whose balance runs out later starts no machines until credit is added). Returns 409 `no_capacity`, with the nearest machine in stock as `alternative`, when no cluster supplier has the machine (in the requested regions) now; see GET /clusters/gpu-types. Requires the `instances:write` scope.

get.description: The GPU machines the cluster suppliers can start now, by GPU type and GPUs per machine (1, 2, 4 or 8), in stock first and cheapest first, with the regions that have stock. A create on a machine with nothing in stock is refused with 409 `no_capacity`, naming the nearest machine in stock in `alternative`. Requires the `instances:read` scope.
get.summary: List the machines clusters can start now

delete.description: Deletes the cluster. Every machine is terminated within seconds and stops billing when terminated; the cost stays in your usage. Requires the `instances:write` scope.

get.description: Returns one cluster with its machines, scheduler queues, the queued and running GPU work the head machine last reported, and the cost so far. Requires the `instances:read` scope.

patch.description: Changes the minimum or maximum number of machines or the idle period. Machines are added within seconds when `min_nodes` rises; machines over a lowered `max_nodes` are drained and released. Returns 409 `cluster_deleting` for a cluster being deleted. Requires the `instances:write` scope.

get.description: A kubeconfig whose server is the cluster's Kubernetes API through GPU.ai and whose token is the API key of this request. Requires the `instances:read` scope; kubectl itself needs `instances:write`. The console's download carries a short-lived credential instead (a `gpuai_kc_` token valid for 8 hours, for this cluster and the signed-in user only), which the Kubernetes route accepts in place of an API key.
get.summary: Get a kubeconfig for a cluster

get.description: Forwards to the cluster's Kubernetes API with full rights in the cluster. Use it through kubectl with the kubeconfig from `/clusters/{id}/kubeconfig`. Every method is forwarded; GET and POST are listed. Exec and attach are not available. Requires the `instances:write` scope.

parameters.description: Any Kubernetes API path, such as api/v1/pods.
parameters.name: path

post.description: Forwards to the cluster's Kubernetes API (see GET).

get.description: Lists the KAI scheduler queues with their priority, GPU quota and limit, and the GPUs each uses and has waiting. Requires the `instances:read` scope.

delete.description: Deletes a queue. The default queue cannot be deleted. Requires the `instances:write` scope.

parameters.description: The queue's name (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens).
parameters.name: name

put.description: Sets a queue. Pods choose it with the label `kai.scheduler/queue` and `schedulerName: kai-scheduler`. `gpu_quota` is the GPUs the queue is guaranteed and `gpu_limit` the most it may use (-1 for none); work over the limit waits until the queue's own work frees GPUs, and adds no machines. Requires the `instances:write` scope.
put.summary: Create or update a scheduler queue

get.description: Forwards to the cluster's Ray dashboard. Use `https://api.gpu.ai/v1/clusters/{id}/ray` as the address of `ray job submit` with the API key in an Authorization header. post.description:
Queues a batch job: a container image, a command, and the GPU it needs. The platform places it on a machine in your organization's job pool, starting a machine when none has room, and terminates machines that have been empty for a few minutes. Requires the `instances:write` scope, because a job can start a machine.

Three opt-ins decide how the job is placed. `max_wait_seconds` lets the job wait for space on a machine you are already paying for before a new one is started. `allow_sharing` lets the job run on the same GPU as other jobs from your own organization. A GPU is never shared with another customer. `allow_restart` lets the platform stop and rerun the job, which sharing needs.

A job shares a GPU only when `allow_sharing` and `allow_restart` are both true and its memory is known, from `memory_hint_mb` or from the peaks of earlier finished jobs with the same name or image. Any other job gets a whole GPU.

Sharing is also limited by compute. Jobs share a GPU only while the sum of their expected compute duties (the share of time each keeps the GPU busy) stays at or under 100%, so two jobs that saturate the GPU never share one. A job's duty comes from `compute_hint_pct` or from the measured utilization of earlier finished jobs with the same name or image. A job with neither counts as 100% and gets a GPU to itself until it has been measured.

The memory reservation is not a hard cap. A job that exits out of GPU memory, or that is stopped for outgrowing its reservation on a full GPU, is run again with a larger reservation, then with a whole GPU, up to `max_retries`. Every job gets a checkpoint directory that survives those reruns on the same machine.

Billing: the machines a job runs on are instances of your organization and are billed like any instance. `attributed_cost_usd` on the job is its share of that, for display.

Free trial: when this deployment runs one, an organization's first jobs are free up to a cap (GET /jobs/trial). Their attributed cost is credited back to the balance as they run.

No balance: an organization with no balance is refused (402) unless the deployment runs the free trial for organizations with no balance and GET /jobs/trial reports `funding` "no_deposit". Then the job runs on the trial with `trial_funded` true. When the trial credit is used the job is cancelled with the status reason "Stopped because your free Jobs trial credit ran out. Add credits to keep running jobs."

GPUAI-Hint.description: Advisory only. Sent while the organization's first jobs are free (GET /jobs/trial), e.g. "Your first jobs are free, up to $10. We credit back what they cost as they run." For a job that runs on the trial with no balance it says the job stops when the trial credit is used.

get.description:
Returns GPU.ai's own price and obtainable capacity for one GPU model over a window, at 15-minute or daily resolution. Requires the `market:read` scope (or `full_access`).

THE NULL CONTRACT. `price_per_gpu_hour` and `available_count` are nullable, and the two states are different facts that must not be collapsed:

* a real `0` means we sampled that bucket and the market was sold out;
* `null` means we did NOT sample that bucket — a failed poll, a skipped cycle, an incident on our side. It says nothing about supply.

The response materializes the full bucket grid across the window, so a gap has visible width. Do not interpolate across a null: that asserts a continuity the data does not have, and reading one as a zero reports our own outages as supplier stockouts.

PER-GPU NORMALIZATION. `price_per_gpu_hour` is always a per-GPU rate. When it was divided out of a whole-node price, `node_price_per_hour` and `gpu_count` are present and describe that derivation; they are absent for single-GPU capacity. A per-GPU figure presented without that context implies single-GPU rentability that whole-node capacity does not offer.

WINDOW CAPS. `bucket=1d` is capped at 365 days (the retention window). `bucket=15m` is capped at 90 days when BOTH `region` and `capacity_class` are supplied, and at 31 days when either is omitted, because an unscoped 15-minute series scans every region and class in every bucket. An over-wide window is a 400 naming the cap and both escapes, never a silent truncation.

This series carries no upstream supplier identity of any kind: the price is GPU.ai's own floor and the count is an aggregate.

Only shapes we actually sell are accepted: an arbitrary integer would return an empty series indistinguishable from a genuine gap, and this surface exists so "no data" and "nothing to have data about" are never the same answer. Use available_cluster_sizes from the response to populate a picker — it reports what this GPU was actually listed as in this window, which is narrower than what we may ever sell.

registry.description: Registry host the login belongs to.

get.description: Lists the organization's secrets by name with their metadata. Values are never returned by any read. Requires the `instances:read` scope. Returns 503 `secrets_unavailable` when secrets are switched on but no encryption key is configured, and 404 when the feature is off.

post.description: Stores a new secret. The value crosses the wire on create, update and import only, is envelope encrypted at rest, and is never returned. The name is the environment variable the value is delivered as: a letter or underscore, then letters, digits and underscores, 128 characters at most; names starting with GPUAI_ and names the machine itself needs (PATH, HOME, LD_PRELOAD and similar) are refused. Values are at most 32 KB. Returns 409 `name_taken` when the name exists (use PUT to replace a value) and 422 `validation_failed` for a bad name or value. Every create, update, delete and use is recorded in the organization's audit log, without the value. Requires the `instances:write` scope.

Creates or updates many secrets at once, for example the output of `infisical export` or a .env file parsed by the client (the `gpu secrets import` command parses dotenv and Infisical JSON locally and sends this request). Every item is validated before any is written. With `overwrite` false, existing secrets are left untouched and listed under `skipped`. At most 200 items. Requires the `instances:write` scope.

200.description: What the import did, by name.

delete.description: Deletes the secret. Machines already running keep the value they were given; nothing started later can receive it, and a function version or job that still names it fails its next run. Requires the `instances:write` scope.

get.description: Returns one secret's metadata. The value is never returned. Requires the `instances:read` scope. 404 `not_found` when the organization has no secret with this name.

put.description: Sets the secret's value, creating the secret when it does not exist (201) or replacing the value and bumping its version when it does (200). Omit `description` to keep the current one. Machines already running keep the value they were given; launches and calls from now on get the new one. Requires the `instances:write` scope.

get.description: Returns the SSH keys owned by the user the API key was minted by. Org-wide key visibility is an admin capability in the dashboard.

404.description: Already deleted (idempotent)

delete.summary: Delete an SSH key (idempotent — 404 on already-gone per D-07)

post.description: Submit an asynchronous text-to-video generation job. Returns a job object with status `queued`; poll GET /videos/{id} until `completed`, then stream the result from GET /videos/{id}/content. Pass an `Idempotency-Key` header to make a retried request replay the original response without a second charge.

get.description: Streams the generated MP4 for a completed job. Returns 410 Gone once the artifact has expired (24h retention).
Lists this organization's watch rules. Requires the `watch:read` scope (or `full_access`). Rules belonging to other organizations are never returned.

post.description:
Creates a rule that notifies you when the market moves on a GPU model. Requires the `watch:write` scope (or `full_access`).

A watch rule ONLY notifies. It cannot launch capacity and cannot spend money: there is no field on this resource that provisions anything. Automatic launching is a separate resource with its own spend-consent gate.

Targeting is dimensional — a GPU model plus optional canonical region and capacity class. It is deliberately NOT possible to pin a rule to a specific catalog listing: listing identity is unstable, so a pinned rule can silently match nothing and never fire.

Delivery is to the organization's registered webhook endpoints, plus an email to the rule's creator. `webhook_endpoint_override_id` routes one rule to one specific endpoint and is the id of an endpoint already registered via `/webhook-endpoints` — the resource accepts no URL of any kind.

Organizations are limited to 50 ENABLED rules; the 422 names the limit.

422.description: Validation failed — a gpu_model that is not a GPU model we list (the detail names the closest ids when there are any), an unknown condition kind, a non-canonical region, a missing threshold on a threshold condition, an override id that is not an endpoint registered by this organization, a field naming a catalog listing or a delivery address, or the enabled-rule limit already reached.

delete.description: Deletes a watch rule. Requires the `watch:write` scope (or `full_access`). Deleting an already-deleted rule returns 404.

get.description: Fetches one watch rule. Requires the `watch:read` scope (or `full_access`). A rule belonging to another organization returns 404 — the same answer as an id that does not exist.

patch.description:
Partially updates a watch rule. Requires the `watch:write` scope (or `full_access`).

An ABSENT key keeps the stored value; an explicit `null` on `region`, `capacity_class` or `webhook_endpoint_override_id` CLEARS it back to "any" / "organization default". The two are distinguished by which keys the body carries, so send only the keys you mean to change.

Editing a rule RE-ARMS it: the fired latch describes the condition that was replaced, so carrying it across an edit would suppress the first alert on the new one.

422.description: Validation failed against the MERGED rule — for example switching to a threshold condition on a rule that has no stored threshold, or re-targeting the rule at a gpu_model we do not list. A gpu_model already stored is only re-checked when the key is SENT, so a rule can always be parked or deleted whatever it holds.

get.description: The starting environments a workspace can be created from, with the Python packages each installs into the workspace. Requires the `instances:read` scope.
Lists the organization's workspaces with status and cost so far. Requires the `instances:read` scope.

post.description: Creates a browser IDE workspace (a VS Code compatible editor, a terminal and JupyterLab) on a GPU machine and starts it. The caller becomes its owner; only the owner can open it. GPU time is billed like an instance while it runs, and its saved folder is billed for storage. Returns 422 `validation_failed` for a bad field, 409 `name_taken` or `limit_reached`, and 409 `no_capacity` (with the nearest GPU in stock as `alternative`) when no supplier has the GPU now. Requires the `instances:write` scope.

get.description: The GPU machines the workspace suppliers can start now, by GPU type and GPUs per machine, in stock first and cheapest first. A create or start on a GPU with nothing in stock is refused with 409 `no_capacity`, naming the nearest GPU in stock in `alternative`. Requires the `instances:read` scope.
get.summary: List the GPUs workspaces can start on now

delete.description: Deletes the workspace. Its machine is released without saving and its saved folder is deleted. Requires the `instances:write` scope.

get.description: Returns one workspace with its recent machines and its GPU and storage cost so far. Requires the `instances:read` scope.

patch.description: Sets `idle_timeout`, the seconds without use after which the workspace saves and stops. Requires the `instances:write` scope.

post.description: Returns a one-time link, valid for two minutes, that logs the owner into the IDE (no port) or into a private app link to `port` inside the workspace. Only the workspace's owner can open it (403 `not_owner`). Requires the `instances:write` scope.
post.summary: Open a workspace or an app link

post.description: Starts a stopped workspace with its saved folder. Pass another `gpu_type` (or an `offering_id`) to switch GPU. Returns 409 `not_stopped` unless the workspace is stopped or failed. Requires the `instances:write` scope.
Saves the workspace folder (including Python packages installed into it) and releases the machine, which stops its GPU billing. Requires the `instances:write` scope.
